description: Fully SYNTHETIC high-net-worth household used by the SlipSlopes demo. No value comes from the Kaggle/personal-finance dataset or from any real client.

provenance_notes.holdings: Synthetic household from the SlipSlopes presentation ($1.80M paper assets).
provenance_notes.stress: Scenario assumption: 2022-style equity drawdown path (linear to trough, hold, partial recovery).
provenance_notes.betas: Scenario assumption: sensitivity of each asset's value to the equity drawdown.
provenance_notes.sbl: Synthetic loan balance; advance rate / maintenance threshold come from the synthetic SBL agreement.
provenance_notes.capital_calls: Scenario assumption: the synthetic LPA leaves call timing to GP discretion.
provenance_notes.rsu: Synthetic vest; withholding rate from the synthetic RSU grant; effective tax rate is an assumption. Household policy assumption: in open trading windows, vested RSUs are sold to keep 3 months of net spending in cash.
provenance_notes.redemptions: Household plan: amounts requested from the REIT and interval fund (resubmitted until filled).
provenance_notes.demand: Scenario assumption: aggregate redemption demand from all investors as % of NAV. No supplied document discloses this; it determines the pro-rata fill rate.
provenance_notes.board: Scenario assumption: share of the 2%/5% cap the board actually honours. The prospectus says the board may repurchase fewer shares or none; 100% means the board fills up to the caps.
